Access requires administrator privileges. Output includes both active and soft-deleted files dependent on filter input. For each result, attachment status, full technical details, and creation/update/deletion audit fields are provided. operations.description:

The returned information includes the user-supplied original filename, internal storage filename and location, exact byte size, MIME type, and a checksum used for duplicate detection and security auditing. Administrative and compliance fields such as deletion timestamp and audit trails (created and updated timestamps) are provided to support management, traceability, and potential audit requirements.

Only non-deleted attachments may be retrieved; requests for missing, deleted, or invalid attachmentId values generate not-found errors. This operation serves both UI file viewers and any back-end correction, compliance, or auditing workflow that requires full file details. This endpoint does not directly store the file's binary data but saves a metadata abstraction for subsequent business linking (e.g., to articles or comments). Internally, duplicate files (with matching checksum) are prevented at the storage/provider layer, and orphan cleanup routines may be triggered post-upload as required.
operations.description:
Registers and records technical metadata for a new file or image uploaded to the discussion board platform. This call initializes a persistent attachment entry, storing user-provided details and internal storage references.

Upon upload, the system captures and stores metadata including the original and internal filenames, file size in bytes, MIME type, and a cryptographically secure SHA-256 checksum used to detect duplicates and support security compliance. The storage provider location (local path or cloud bucket) is also recorded, ensuring the backend can manage the attachment lifecycle independently from any business object (e.g., article, comment).

File creation and update audit timestamps are set on record creation. Validation enforces file size and MIME type requirements, and checks for duplicate files using the checksum. Invalid or already-present files are rejected with descriptive error codes, supporting best practices for attachment management, compliance, and audit readiness. This operation does not link the file to any business entity; such associations are managed in downstream tables and logic.

All changes are logged using the updated_at audit field for compliance and troubleshooting purposes. operations.description:

The operation enforces strict field validations per the Prisma schema to prevent impossible, malicious, or contradictory changes. All changes are captured via the updated_at field, supporting forensic audit and root-cause analysis if problems arise. An attempt to update non-editable or critical identity fields (e.g., id, checksum_sha256, created_at) will result in a validation error.

Proper authorization is required, typically restricted to system administrators. File content and business associations (such as article linkage) are managed through other business-layer operations, not directly in this endpoint.

IDiscussionBoardUser.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for registering a new discussion board user account.

Used in the join/registration endpoint to create a new persistent identity in the system. All fields must correspond exactly with the underlying discussion_board_users schema fields. This DTO captures the user's core authentication fields as mandatory for account creation. System-managed fields and authentication context (such as account ID or session info) are excluded. No unlisted properties should be included; only use schema-confirmed fields for security and correctness.

Credential fields must use plain text (for passwords), which are hashed server-side before storage. Email uniqueness and any password policies are enforced by the backend and validation layer. This DTO does NOT include actor or session context fields, as registration for this entity does not use authenticated context. Optional Prisma fields may be omitted or included as null if applicable.

email.description: User's unique email address for registration and login. Used for authentication and as a natural key; must be unique across all user accounts in the system. Validated for RFC 5322 compliance.

password.description: Plain-text password chosen by the user for initial registration. Subject to minimum length and complexity enforcement, with actual hash stored in the password_hash field in the database. Never stored or accepted in hashed form from the client. Value is handled safely server-side according to security best practices.

IDiscussionBoardUser.IAuthorized.description:
Authentication response payload after a successful login or refresh for a discussion board user.

This object contains the unique user ID (uuid as per database schema), and an authorization token object. The response is issued only on successful authentication and should never be returned if login/refresh fails.

The token field must be a named $ref. The ID must match the database user ID.

id.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the authenticated discussion board user. This directly corresponds to the id field in discussion_board_users.

email.description:
User's unique email address for registration and login.

Serves as both authentication credential and natural key for de-duplication. Must be unique across all users. Used for correspondence, notifications, and system audit. Email uniqueness and formatting are strictly enforced by both the database and application layer.

created_at.description:
Timestamp of account creation, as stored in discussion_board_users.created_at.

Set at the moment the user registers. Immutable after creation. Used for audit, reporting, and lifecycle management.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of last update or modification to user account (discussion_board_users.updated_at).

Reflects changes to user profile data, password modification, or administrative actions. Read-only in API response; set automatically.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp marking the account as soft-deleted; null if active. Sourced from discussion_board_users.deleted_at.

If the account has been soft-deleted by admin, this field contains the deletion timestamp. If null, user account is active. Used in access checks, reporting, and account recovery/audit.
No deletion recorded; account is active. 'deleted_at' is null in discussion_board_users table.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp marking the account as soft-deleted (or null if active).

IDiscussionBoardUser.ILogin.description:
Login request credentials for a discussion board user. This schema strictly defines the required fields for user authentication based on the actual columns in the discussion_board_users table and supporting session business logic.

Authentication is performed solely using the email and password fields; these must match confirmed user records as validated by the schema and backend logic. Password is supplied in plain text for backend hashing and credential verification.

Session context fields (href and referrer) are required to ensure platform auditability, security tracing, and compliance with abuse investigation requirements. They must be supplied by the client for every login attempt, with full URL and referrer values. The ip field is included as optional for additional audit trace if not set automatically by the server.

There are no extra IDs, surrogates, or assumed fields present; all included fields correspond directly to business, security, and traceability needs as enforced by requirements and implementation.

email.description: User's unique email address for login and account identity, as recorded in discussion_board_users. Required for credential validation and must conform to RFC 5322.

password.description: Plain-text password provided by the user for authentication. Backend will hash and verify this against the password_hash column in the database; the value should never be logged or exposed beyond the authentication process.

oneOf.description: Client's IP address recorded as part of session metadata. Optional; can be omitted or set to null to indicate that the backend server will provide it.
Null value if the client did not supply IP or if server auto-records. Keeps audit context flexible for various client/server deployment environments.

ip.description: Optional client-side IP address for augmenting session context and platform audit trails. Nullable for deployment flexibility.

href.description: Full URL requested by the user at the initiation of authentication. This is required for comprehensive audit logging and abuse detection.

referrer.description: Full HTTP referrer supplied by client at login, required for audit and abuse traceability. Must always be a non-empty URI.

IDiscussionBoardUser.IRefresh.description:
Refresh token payload for persistent JWT session management.

This type is used exclusively to request new access/refresh tokens for an authenticated session, and accepts only the refresh token assigned to a valid session. Credentials and user identity fields are strictly forbidden to protect the authentication lifecycle and API minimalism. The design adheres to all operational and security requirements, ensuring only supported properties are accepted.

No additional fields, metadata, or keys are permitted; this schema is purpose-built for secure JWT refresh operations.

token.description: Refresh token associated with the user's persistent session. Must match a server-issued token for continued authentication. Absolutely required for the refresh flow.

email.description:
Unique email address for administrator registration and authentication.

Must be unique among all admin accounts. Used for login and compliance tracking. Validated to ensure a proper email format. Distinct from user emails—admins and users have fully separated credential spaces in the system. See discussion_board_admins.email schema comment.

password.description:
Administrator password to be hashed and securely stored.

The client provides this as plain text; backend hashes with BCrypt prior to storage in password_hash. Minimum 8 characters per security requirements. The password is never stored nor exposed in plain form at any time. Mapped to password_hash in the database but exposed to the API only as 'password' for clarity and security. See discussion_board_admins.password_hash schema comment.

oneOf.description: Client IP address for session tracking. Optional—server will extract if not provided, but can be supplied for SSR or advanced logging.
Client IP address for session tracking. Optional—server will extract if not provided, but can be supplied for SSR or advanced logging.

ip.description: Client IP address for auditing, security, and compliance. Optional—if omitted, the backend extracts IP from the HTTP request context. Used for compliance logging of admin join operations. May be supplied if known in client-side rendering or proxy environments.

href.description:
URL of the page where the admin joined.

This field records the current page (connection URL) at the time of account creation for advanced auditing and compliance. This is mandatory and must be provided by the client. See security and audit requirements for session context fields.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL that led to the admin registration page.

Mandatory field for compliance and audit logging. This is used to reconstruct the join flow for moderation, security review, and regulatory purposes. Must be a valid URI or an empty string if direct navigation occurred.

IDiscussionBoardAdmin.IJoin.description:
Administrator registration request type for the discussion board platform.

Represents the required information for registering a new board admin. The client must provide a unique email, a plain-text password (hashed for storage), and session context fields (href, referrer, and optional ip). This DTO is mapped to the discussion_board_admins table and is compliant with strict security and audit requirements as described in the database schema comments.

Email and password are required to create the admin account. Session context fields are critical for compliance and advanced audit trails. Admins created with this type are immediately eligible for privileged access and further authentication operations.

IDiscussionBoardAdmin.IAuthorized.description:
Administrator authentication success response. Represents an authorized admin session with issued JWT tokens and the admin's unique identity information.

Returned by both login and refresh endpoints for admin authentication, this DTO conveys the identity of the authenticated board administrator and contains newly issued JWT tokens (RFC 7519-compliant). The token information references the IAuthorizationToken type to encapsulate access/refresh tokens, expiry, and associated metadata.

This schema excludes all sensitive database fields such as password_hash and internal flags. The properties focus on providing the bare minimum of admin information along with current authentication context.

id.description: Unique UUID identifier for the authenticated admin, matching the id of the discussion_board_admins record.

email.description: The admin's unique email address, confirming successful authentication and reflecting the current account.

created_at.description: Date and time when the admin account was created. Set automatically upon account creation.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the last modification to the administrator account. Updated whenever profile or password changes occur.

deleted_at.description: Soft delete marker (nullable). Null if this account is active; date-time value if account is deactivated. Used for audit, compliance, and recovery.

IDiscussionBoardAdmin.ILogin.description:
Administrator login request DTO for authenticating moderator access to the discussion board management system.

This schema represents the credentials used by a registered board administrator to log in. It includes the email address (which uniquely identifies the admin) and the plaintext password for secure verification against the bcrypt hash in the database. The fields mapped here directly reflect business logic constraints and audit policies defined in the Prisma schema.

The credentials are checked for correspondence with a valid, non-deleted administrator account. The fields in this schema must be provided as raw form data for credential verification and privilege identification.

email.description: Unique email address for the administrator logging in. This must match an active admin account and will be used as the primary identifier during authentication. Enforced as unique among all admin records in the database.

password.description: The plaintext password for the admin's login attempt. This value is compared against the stored bcrypt password_hash for authentication. Must meet internal password policy for administrators, typically minimum 8 characters; exact policy may be enforced in implementation.

IDiscussionBoardAdmin.IRefresh.description:
DTO for admin authentication token refresh.

This schema represents a request to renew JWT access/refresh tokens for an active admin session. The refresh token value must correspond to a valid session record in the admin session table. This operation does not require the admin's email/password; only the issued refresh token is needed.

The server verifies the token's validity and its association with a non-deleted administrator account before issuing new authentication tokens.

refresh_token.description: Issued refresh token value for admin identity renewal. Must be valid and correspond to an active session as tracked in the discussion_board_admin_sessions table.

This type is used for privileged administrative operations that update user data, such as correcting email addresses, reactivating accounts, or auditing account data. Field-level validation is enforced to protect the unique nature of email addresses, and to guarantee accurate tracking of account modifications. IDiscussionBoardUserSession.description:
Represents a single login session record for a discussion board user.

This entity tracks a user's authenticated login event. It is primarily used for audit trails, session validation, and administrative investigation or revocation. Session records are immutable from the user's perspective and can only be updated or revoked by administrators, providing an audit-safe record of session activity.

Each session maintains metadata including IP address, the full request URL (href) when the session was initiated, and the HTTP referrer. These properties help establish traceability for both user experience diagnostics and abuse/security investigation.

In the API response, the session is linked to its parent user via a user summary object (user: IDiscussionBoardUser.ISummary), supporting multiple concurrent sessions per user and providing complete context for administrative/audit operations. Session expiration is tracked by the expired_at property. Usage includes administrative session audits, compliance checks, and targeted logoff or revocation actions.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the session record.

Used as the primary key in the database table. Uniquely distinguishes individual session records.

user.description:
Summary of the user who owns this session.

Transformed from the database foreign key user_id. Provides administrative/audit interfaces with complete contextual user information in a single API call, following .ISummary association rules.

ip.description:
IP address captured at session start.

Used for traceability, audit investigation, and abuse/threat analysis. Stored in original string format without transformation.

href.description:
The full request URL (href) seen by the server during login/authentication.

Useful for reconstructing client navigation context and investigating possible session fixation or redirection attacks.

referrer.description:
HTTP referrer value at time of session creation.

Captures the previous page/location leading to this session's initiation, supporting audit of legitimate or suspicious login flows.

created_at.description:
Timestamp of session record creation (login time).

Used for security analysis and audit trails.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp for when the session expired or was terminated (logout time or forced expiration).

Null if the session is still currently active. Administrators may set this value to end a session for compliance, security, or operational policy reasons.

IDiscussionBoardUserSession.IUpdate.description:
DTO for updating a discussion board user's session record, used exclusively by administrative APIs for forced session termination, metadata adjustment, or expiration extension.

This type allows privileged admins to update select fields in a session record. The only updatable property is expired_at, which can be set to mark the session as terminated. All other properties are immutable for security and auditability. This type intentionally excludes the primary key, foreign key, and immutable creation fields to prevent unauthorized modifications and maintain a secure, audit-safe session history.

Used in endpoints for admin-driven session state changes (e.g., forced logoff) or compliance-driven adjustments.

Never exposed directly to users or non-privileged clients.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp to set session expiration or forced termination.

May be set to a valid date-time string to expire the session or null to indicate the session is still active. Only privileged admins may update this field.

id.description: Unique identifier for the administrator account. This UUID value is the primary key in the database for referencing and managing admin records.

email.description: Unique administrator email address for login and identity verification. Must be unique among all admin accounts and cannot overlap with user emails. Used for authentication and correspondence.

created_at.description: Date and time when the admin account was created. Set automatically upon account creation.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the last modification to the administrator account. Updated whenever profile or password changes occur.

deleted_at.description: Soft delete marker (nullable). Null if this account is active; date-time value if account is deactivated. Used for audit, compliance, and recovery.

IDiscussionBoardAdmin.description:
Administrator entity representing privileged accounts responsible for system governance and moderation.

Admins are uniquely identified by email addresses and have platform-wide rights to manage content and users. Account creation, modification, and soft deletion are recorded via timestamps. The Prisma model enforces email uniqueness and password security. The password hash is never exposed in any public interface or API response.

This schema is used for profile read operations (`GET /discussionBoard/admin/admins/{adminId}`) and as a basis for record updates. Sensitive data like the password hash is always excluded from external APIs.

email.description: Filter field: exact or partial match on administrator email address. Enables searching for admins by email. Optional in search; may be omitted to find all accounts.

created_after.description: Lower time boundary for admin accounts created after this timestamp. Used for filtering by account creation date. Optional; if omitted, no lower bound is applied.

created_before.description: Upper time boundary for accounts created before this time. Enables filtering admin list by account creation date. Optional; if omitted, no upper bound is applied.

updated_after.description: Lower time boundary for accounts updated after this timestamp. Enables filtering administrator list by last activity. Optional search parameter.

updated_before.description: Upper boundary for accounts updated before this time. Combined with updated_after for interval-based search. Optional.

deleted.description: Search condition for admin deletion status: true to show only deactivated (soft-deleted) admins, false to show only active, or omit for all. Optional.

page.description: Page number to display. 1-based, for paginated admin searches. Optional; defaults to first page.

limit.description: Number of results per page (pagination limit). Must be between 1 and 100. Optional; defaults as defined by API.

oneOf.description: Field to sort admin search results by. Enum: 'email', 'created_at', or 'updated_at'. Optional; defaults to internal sort policy.

IDiscussionBoardAdmin.IRequest.description:
API search/filter criteria for querying administrator accounts registered in the system.

This schema is used for paginated, filtered, and sorted admin directory searches. All fields are optional, enabling flexible query composition for administrative dashboards.

Each field directly corresponds to a searchable property in the discussion_board_admins table. Pagination and sorting fields support standard list browsing patterns for administrator entities.

IDiscussionBoardAdmin.IUpdate.description:
Payload for updating administrator account profile in the discussion board system.

This schema supports modifications to mutable administrator properties such as email, password, and account status (soft deletion/reactivation). It is used exclusively for privileged administrative actions on the 'discussion_board_admins' table. All fields correspond to actual columns in the database and are subject to validation, uniqueness, and system security rules.

Excludes immutable fields such as creation timestamp. Password must always be supplied via the plain 'password' field; the hash is backend-managed and never sent by client. 'deleted_at' controls account deactivation when set, or reactivation when set to null. Changing the password rotates credentials and triggers audit logging.

email.description: Administrator's unique email address. Changing this field requires the new address to be valid and unique among all administrators. Used for login and notifications.

password.description: Plain text password for administrator authentication. Sent only when a password change or reset is desired. The password must be at least 8 characters and is securely hashed and stored by the backend. Never send a pre-hashed value.

oneOf.description: Soft-delete timestamp in ISO 8601 UTC format. Set to the current datetime to deactivate the admin account. Set explicitly to null to reactivate. Created_at is immutable and never altered.
Set to null for reactivation of a previously deleted account.

deleted_at.description: Soft-delete timestamp for account deactivation/reactivation. Allow null to reactivate. Must use ISO 8601 UTC format if present.

IDiscussionBoardAdminSession.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for searching or filtering administrator session records ('discussion_board_admin_sessions').

Used to support paginated or filtered queries for session logs under a given admin account. All properties correspond to filterable fields in the session database schema. Timestamps must use ISO 8601 UTC format. Null or omission of properties disables filtering on that field. Supports advanced audit/search use cases when reviewing account access history.

ip.description: Filter by IP address of the administrator login session. Optional; match exact IP string if provided.

href.description: Filter by authentication request URL (href) at session establishment. Optional; match exact string if provided.

referrer.description: Filter by HTTP referrer at session authentication. Optional; match exact string if provided.

created_at_from.description: Lower bound filter for creation timestamp. Return sessions created at or after this time. ISO 8601 UTC format.

created_at_to.description: Upper bound filter for creation timestamp. Return sessions created at or before this time. ISO 8601 UTC format.

expired_at_from.description: Lower bound filter for session expiry timestamp. Return sessions expiring at or after this time. ISO 8601 UTC format.

expired_at_to.description: Upper bound filter for session expiry timestamp. Return sessions expiring at or before this time. ISO 8601 UTC format.

page.description: Page number for pagination. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of session records per page. Defaults to 20. Hard limit of 100.

IDiscussionBoardAdminSession.description:
Administrator login session entity used throughout the discussion board system for security audit and administrative compliance workflows.

Each instance represents a distinct session for an authenticated administrator, capturing their login event, session context, IP address, request/referrer flow, and lifecycle timestamps. Sessions are fundamental for recording administrative privilege escalations and providing full traceability of sensitive access events.

Relationships include:
- Parent admin context (via id and embedded summary) for privilege traceability and incident response
- Session events tracked for compliance enforcement, audit reporting, and privilege lifecycle monitoring

The session record supports advanced administrative operations such as session force-expiry, incident investigation, and session enumeration for security reviews. Lifecycle fields enable tracking of active, expired, or forcibly terminated sessions as required by policy. This schema is core for regulatory audit, privileged access reconciliation, and platform compliance reporting workflows.

id.description: Unique identifier for the administrator session record. Serves as the immutable session primary key. Generated at session creation time using UUID v4. Used as a foreign key for audit trail and privilege escalation logs.

admin.description:
Summary information of the administrator account owning this session.

References the parent administrator via embedded summary DTO (see IDiscussionBoardAdmin.ISummary for audit context). Used to attribute session events, privilege escalations, and incident investigations to the responsible administrator. Never includes sensitive credentials or authentication secrets in this reference.

ip.description:
IP address from which the login session was established.

Captured and stored for auditing, malicious activity detection, and investigation of unauthorized access. Also supports correlation to network logs in compliance workflows.

href.description:
URL (href) of the login/authentication request that created this session.

Used to reconstruct the activity flow and origin context for security, audit, and debugging purposes, enabling full user journey analysis for compliance investigations.

referrer.description:
HTTP referrer URL indicating the navigation source before the authentication request.

Essential for determining how administrators accessed the login, helps with monitoring user flows, detecting phishing, or replay attacks in compliance reviews.

created_at.description:
Timestamp for when this session was established (login event).

Recorded in UTC ISO 8601 format. Used in all audit, compliance, and incident response reports. Immutable after creation.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp for when the session was terminated (either normal expiry or forced logout).

Null indicates an active session. Non-null values mark a completed session lifecycle and are critical for compliance reconciliation and security operations.

IDiscussionBoardAdminSession.IUpdate.description:
Update object for administrative session lifecycle control in regulated environments.

Primarily used in force-expiry or incident remediation flows, allowing privileged operators to set or clear the session expiration timestamp in accordance with incident response or operational policy.

Requires full audit logging and careful compliance validation. The DTO never permits privilege escalation or creation/deletion of session objects, only explicit lifecycle changes under administrative review.

expired_at.description:
New session expiration timestamp to mark forced expiry or session closure.

Set to current time for forced logout or null to activate/validate session as ongoing. Always triggers audit reporting workflow and compliance handler checks.

IDiscussionBoardAdmin.ISummary.description:
Summary data for a registered system administrator account in the discussion board.

Provides enough identifying and audit information for list views, references, and minimal embedding. Excludes sensitive fields such as password hashes. Used for referencing admins in audit logs, moderation actions, and lists. Never returns sensitive fields, authentication credentials, or internal details.

Maintains traceability for privilege assignment and operational auditing. Designed for performance and API consistency. Based on the discussion_board_admins Prisma model.

id.description: Unique identifier for the administrator account. Generated automatically upon creation. Used as a foreign key in admin references across the system.

email.description: Administrator's unique email address. Used for authentication and identification in the admin panel and logs.

created_at.description: Datetime when this administrator account was created, in ISO 8601 UTC format. Never changes after creation.

updated_at.description: Datetime when this administrator's data was last updated.

deleted_at.description:
Soft-delete marker for this administrator.

When null, the account is active and visible in all admin-selection and auditing interfaces. When set to a valid datetime, the account has been soft-deleted—privileges and visibility are restricted, but the entry is retained for compliance, operational trace, and audit trail review.

This field is used to implement logical deletion: no record is ever physically removed, ensuring accountability for all admin actions throughout the board's history.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for filtering, sorting, and paginating article results in the discussion_board_articles table.

Allows clients to specify criteria such as article title (partial match), author ID, creation or update date range, soft delete status, sort criteria, and pagination info. Supports comprehensive searching, listing, and browsing use cases for the main discussion board article entity.

Fields should follow validation rules: trimming for strings, UUID format for identifiers, and ISO 8601 for dates. Exceeding limits or invalid formats must be handled as validation errors.

title.description: Optional filter for article title partial match (case-insensitive). Whitespace-trimmed, internally sanitized. If provided, used as a substring search on the 'title' field.

author_user_id.description: Optional filter for articles by a specific author. Corresponds to the user_id in discussion_board_articles. Must be a valid UUID. When omitted, articles by all authors are included.

created_from.description: Optional start of the creation datetime filter (inclusive, ISO 8601 format). Only articles created at or after this datetime are included. Null or omitted means no lower bound.

created_to.description: Optional end of the creation datetime filter (inclusive, ISO 8601 format). Only articles created at or before this datetime are included. Null or omitted means no upper bound.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.description:
Main detail view of a single article in discussion_board_articles.

Represents all business-facing fields present in the article table: includes the article ID (UUID), title, content, author reference, and audit fields (creation, last update, deletion timestamp). Follows soft-delete pattern: deleted_at is null for visible/active articles and has an ISO 8601 datetime for soft-deleted articles. Author relationship is exposed as an object reference (IDiscussionBoardUser.ISummary) to support atomic read and avoid N+1 queries (never expose raw FK for contextual references).

Fields follow all constraints from the Prisma schema: title max 200 characters, content max 10,000 characters, all timestamps as ISO strings, and id validated as UUIDs. Attachments and history are accessible in subsidiary or related endpoints/types, and are not embedded directly here.

id.description: Unique identifier for the article (UUID, system-generated).

title.description: Title of the article. Required. Maximum 200 characters (see schema-level constraint), whitespace-trimmed and sanitized.

content.description: Full text body of the article. Required. Maximum 10,000 characters. Only plain text allowed; no HTML markup supported.

author.description: Detailed information of the user who authored this article. Reference to the user entity as an object for atomic data retrieval; enables immediate display of author profile fields in all article detail responses. Never show raw UUID FKs for contextual references.

created_at.description: Date/time the article was created (ISO 8601 UTC). Never changes after creation.

updated_at.description: Date/time of the last update to the article, including content or attachments (ISO 8601 UTC).

oneOf.description: Soft delete timestamp as ISO 8601 datetime if the article is deleted (null if not deleted).

deleted_at.description: Soft delete field: null if active, otherwise contains deletion datetime for traceability.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.ICreate.description:
Data transfer object (DTO) for creating a new article in the discussion board system.

Clients use this schema when submitting new posts. The request requires a plain text title (max 200 characters, trimmed and sanitized) and plain text content (max 10,000 characters). The authenticated user's identity is automatically linked on the backend (user_id), so user_id is not present in the DTO. Audit fields (created_at/updated_at) are system-managed and therefore also absent.

All validation rules for lengths, sanitation, and text format are enforced based on the requirements and database schema.

Upon creation, attachments are not included. Separate operations handle article attachments if necessary.

title.description: Title of the article. Plain text only, maximum 200 characters. Leading and trailing whitespace will be trimmed on the server. Must not contain HTML or unsafe content.

content.description: Full body text of the article in plain text. Maximum 10,000 characters. No markdown or HTML allowed, only sanitized plain text.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.IUpdate.description:
DTO for article update requests in the discussion board system.

Represents permissible fields for partial or complete update of an existing article. Typical use includes editing the title and body content post-creation as allowed by the business logic and access controls.

System-managed fields—including id, user_id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at—are strictly omitted from this DTO and are not editable through the API. Update permissions are enforced server-side, and field validation applies length constraints, sanitation, and patch semantics according to business policy. Only authorized users (author/admin) may invoke this operation.

title.description: Title of the article after update. Maximum 200 characters, with trimming and sanitation by backend logic. Optional for partial update; can be null or omitted for no change.

content.description: Full text of the article after update, plain text only, up to 10,000 characters. Must not contain HTML or markdown. Optional for partial update—omit or set null for no change.

IDiscussionBoardArticleAttachment.description:
Metadata and linkage entity for article attachments (images or documents).

Links an uploaded file or image to a specific article, providing file metadata, secure storage URI, and audit information. Attachments are dependent on their parent article (cannot exist stand-alone). Validation for file types, extension, size, and URI is strictly enforced per business and security policy.

All permissions for read and modification are derived via API ownership or administrator access to the parent article. Soft deletion by users or moderators is recorded via the deleted_at timestamp for compliance and moderation trails.

Typical clients display information from this DTO for file preview, secure download rendering, and attachment management UI.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the attachment record (UUID, system-generated at upload).

Used for reference in all attachment operations.

article_id.description:
UUID of the parent article to which this attachment is related.

Foreign key safe for display, never editable by the client; set by the API context.

file_name.description:
Original filename and extension as provided by the uploading user. Used for display, download, and business validation.

Validated against length and forbidden character constraints.

mime_type.description: MIME type of the uploaded file, enforced by file type whitelist for security and rendering behavior. Provided at upload and verified by the backend.

file_size.description:
Uploaded file size in bytes. Range: 1 byte to 10,485,760 bytes (10MB) for validation and quota enforcement.

Zero-length files forbidden; size upper bound set by business rules.

file_uri.description: Storage URI pointing to the uploaded file resource (S3, CDN, or local storage). Never a direct public file path, always controlled via secure access policy.

created_at.description: Datestamp of record creation (UTC). Used for upload tracking, audit, and chronological sorting.

deleted_at.description: Soft delete timestamp, set when moderation, user action, or compliance removes an attachment. Null when active.

page.description: Page number for paginated retrieval of attachments (1-based). Defaults to 1 if not specified.

limit.description: Maximum number of attachment records to return per page. Upper cap is enforced at 50 as per API performance constraints.

search.description: Optional search term for attachment filename filter (matches part or full file_name). Used for filtering to attachments whose filename contains this substring. Case-insensitive. Useful for situations where an article has a large number of attachments.

oneOf.description:
Sorting criteria for the returned attachments. Accepts only 'file_name' (alphabetical), 'created_at' (chronological), or 'file_size' (by file size).

Defaults to 'created_at' if not given.

IDiscussionBoardArticleAttachment.IReque.description:
Parameters for searching, filtering, and paginating article attachments.

Supports retrieval by page, limit, search on original filenames, and sorting by name/date/size as needed for attachment management interfaces.

file_name.description:
Original name of the uploaded file, including the extension (as provided by the user).
This field is validated for allowed file types/extensions (e.g., jpg, jpeg, png, gif, pdf, doc, docx, xls, xlsx, ppt, pptx), size, and non-empty string constraints.
The extension is parsed from this field for business validation and audit purposes.
Must not be empty, must match a permitted extension, and reflects the filename as supplied by the user at upload.

mime_type.description:
MIME type of the upload, as provided by the client and validated server-side (e.g., image/png, application/pdf).
This field is strictly validated against allowed/whitelisted types in business rules and used for security filtering and type assignment.
Must match the file type, not be empty, and support extension-based and content-based detection.

file_size.description:
Attachment size in bytes. Maximum value is 10MB (10 * 1024 * 1024 = 10,485,760 bytes), per requirements.
Value must be greater than zero; empty/zero-length files are forbidden. Used for quota, validation, and audit.

file_uri.description:
Storage URI for the uploaded file (as returned by the storage subsystem during upload phase).
Must be a valid URI string (e.g., S3 URL or internal storage URI), not a file path, and never contain direct access tokens.
End users provide the URI after the secure upload step, ensuring the back-end only receives the reference, not raw data.
This must be provided and validated for secure linking of file objects to the article attachment metadata.

IDiscussionBoardArticleAttachment.ICreat.description:
Attachment upload DTO for the discussion board article attachment system. Used to create a new attachment record (image or document) on an article. 

This object is strictly validated for file name (including extension), MIME type, file size, and URI (pre-uploaded reference, not raw data) per security and business rules. 

Permissions and quota are enforced through backend logic, allowing only valid file types and sizes as specified in requirements. See API documentation for permitted file extensions and types.

DO NOT include actor/user or parent article fields; article context is provided by API path and authentication context, never by user input.

file_name.description:
Original name of the file if updating/replacing the attachment.
Must follow same rules as in ICreate; optional for partial updates/replacement flows.

mime_type.description: MIME type of the upload, as provided by the client and validated server-side. Must follow same business validation rules as in ICreate; optional on partial update.

file_size.description: Size in bytes of the replacement file, if uploading a new one. Value must be within allowed range (1 - 10MB). Optional for metadata-only updates.

file_uri.description: Storage URI for the updated file, if replacing the attachment content. Optional.

oneOf.description: Timestamp for soft deletion of this attachment. If present, marks this attachment as logically deleted in the system. Optional for partial update/replace, but should be set to current timestamp for admin/owner soft-delete action.
Null means attachment remains active. Use explicit ISO8601 date-time string for soft deletion; set null for restoring or keeping the attachment active.

deleted_at.description: Updated soft deletion state for the attachment: if present, marks as deleted; if null or omitted, the attachment remains active.

IDiscussionBoardArticleAttachment.IUpdat.description:
Attachment update DTO for discussion board article attachments. Used when replacing file content, updating attachment metadata, or performing a partial soft-delete (logical delete) on an existing attachment.

All properties are optional to support PATCH/PUT partial updates. To initiate a logical delete, provide the `deleted_at` field with the current UTC timestamp in ISO8601 format. For standard metadata or file updates, omit `deleted_at` or supply null.

Parent/ownership context is strictly controlled in the API path/context, not provided by the user. Partial updates are validated according to attachment business rules and storage policies.

id.description:
Primary key for moderation event. Unique identifier (UUID) for this moderation log entry, providing traceability and immutable identity for all audit and compliance operations.

This value links all retrieval, update, and compliance actions for the specific moderation record.

target_type.description:
Type of thing acted on ("article", "comment", "attachment").

Specifies which core discussion board entity was subject to moderation. Supported values:
- "article": indicates an article/thread was moderated
- "comment": indicates a discussion comment was moderated
- "attachment": indicates an attached file or image was moderated

Valid values reflect the normalized, polymorphic structure for logging moderation of any entity type in this table.

target_id.description:
UUID of the item moderated (article, comment, or attachment).

This value refers to the unique identifier of the entity referenced by target_type. Used for cross-entity polymorphic linking and forensic investigations to tie the moderation to the affected item.

action.description:
Moderation action performed (e.g., "remove", "edit", "ban").

Records the type of administrative or compliance event completed, such as removing content, editing for policy, banning a user or attachment, etc. Populated according to a controlled vocabulary matching valid actions for the target entity type.

Must be sufficient to describe what occurred for audit/compliance purposes.

reason.description:
Reason for this moderation action as entered by the admin.

Human-readable, business-context rationale (e.g., "policy violation: abusive language", "privacy request", "file type not permitted"). May be shown in audit trails and moderator review tools.

outcome.description:
Result or status after moderation (e.g., "deleted", "edited", "banned", "restored").

Summarizes the effect of the moderation or compliance event as realized in the system after the action.

created_at.description:
Timestamp representing when this moderation action was performed (UTC, ISO 8601).

Used for precise ordering, analytics, and legal compliance, ensuring immutable, reliable temporal audit information.

admin_id.description:
Admin account responsible for moderation action. Refers to {@link discussion_board_admins.id}.

This UUID associates this moderation action with the system administrator who performed the event. Used for access control, compliance logging, and accountability.

IDiscussionBoardModerationLog.description:
Moderation log tracking all administrative actions on articles, comments, and attachments.

Each event records the type of action performed (remove, edit, ban, etc.), the target entity (article, comment, or attachment) by ID, the acting admin, action rationale, outcome, and exact timestamp. Supports transparent audit trails and minimal compliance needs for this discussion board. Entries are never deleted to maintain historical traceability.

The log references existing core entities via type+ID, allowing polymorphic tracking of acted-upon items in a normalized, non-redundant way.

action.description: Moderation action (e.g., "remove", "edit") to search for. Optional filter; when supplied, returns only logs for this moderation event type.

outcome.description: Outcome/status (e.g., "deleted", "restored") to filter results by moderation result. Optional.

target_type.description: Optional filter for entity type ("article", "comment", or "attachment"). Returns results only for logs targeting this entity type.

target_id.description: Optional filter for the specific entity affected by moderation. When supplied, returns only log entries matching the specified target UUID.

admin_id.description: Optional filter for actions by a specific admin. When provided, returns only events recorded by this admin account, referencing their unique UUID.

date_from.description: Inclusive start of timestamp filter window (UTC, ISO 8601). Filters for moderation log entries created after or at this time. Optional.

date_to.description: Inclusive end of timestamp filter window (UTC, ISO 8601). Filters for log entries created before or at this time. Optional.

search.description: Free-text search term to match rationale/reason or related fields. Supports broad auditing of moderation events for control/justification review.

page.description: Page number for paginated results (1-based index). Optional; default is 1 if omitted.

limit.description: Maximum number of results per page. Typical systems cap at 100 for efficiency and performance.

sort_by.description: Optional field by which to sort (e.g., "created_at", "action"). Controls result ordering for review and audit processes.

oneOf.description: Sort direction: 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending. Optional. Default is 'desc' to show most recent events first.
Sort direction: 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending. Optional. Default is 'desc' to show most recent events first.

sort_order.description: Sort direction: 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending. Optional. Default is 'desc' to show most recent events first.

IDiscussionBoardModerationLog.IRequest.description:
Search, filter, and pagination parameters for discussion board moderation log retrieval.

Allows administrators or auditors to locate moderation events based on target entity, action, outcome, admin, date ranges, or free-text rationale search. Response is paginated and supports flexible, multi-criteria queries for transparency and traceability. Filtering and sorting fields match Prisma schema, supporting comprehensive compliance needs.

IDiscussionBoardModerationLog.ISummary.description:
Summary DTO for moderation log entries in the discussion board, representing a historical audit trail of all admin actions taken on articles, comments, or attachments.

Each summary contains the full moderation context for a given action: the item type acted upon, its unique identifier, the admin responsible, the action performed, reason and outcome, and precise timestamp of the event. This provides immutable transparency for all user-facing moderation. Log entries allow clients to present quick lists of removal/ban/edit actions, show reasons to affected users, or analyze moderator patterns in administration dashboards.

This summary form is performance-optimized for list or search results and does not include administrator details or target object details in object form, focusing on what happened, to what, by whom, and why. Actual details for referenced objects (articles, comments, attachments, or admins) can be obtained via separate endpoints if required.

id.description: Unique identifier for this moderation event. Primary key of the moderation logs table.

target_type.description: Type of the entity acted upon by this moderation event. One of 'article', 'comment', or 'attachment'. This is a literal string, enabling polymorphic tracking of entity types referenced by target_id.

target_id.description: UUID representing the article, comment, or attachment that was the target of the admin action. Used with target_type to form a polymorphic link.

admin_id.description: Unique identifier of the admin who performed this moderation action. Foreign key to discussion_board_admins.id. See related admin details via lookup if needed.

action.description: The moderation action performed by the admin (for example: 'remove', 'edit', 'ban'). Expresses the administrative intent and effect.

reason.description: Rationale provided by the moderator for this administrative action, describing policy reason or observed issue.

outcome.description: Post-moderation status or result (such as 'deleted', 'edited', 'banned', 'restored'). Used for transparency and analysis.

created_at.description: Timestamp in UTC ISO 8601 format of when the moderation action occurred. Indicates precise audit timing for all administrative events.

IDiscussionBoardModerationLog.ICreate.description:
DTO for creating a new moderation log entry in the discussion_board_moderation_logs table. Used to record all administrative/moderation actions performed by an admin on articles, comments, or attachments in the discussion board system.

Captures essential audit attributes of the moderation event: the type of target entity ("article", "comment", or "attachment"), its unique identifier, the moderation action taken, rationale for the action, outcome, and the exact time the action occurred. The acting admin's identity is provided by authentication context and is NOT present in the request body.

This schema ensures immutability, auditability, and complete traceability for each moderation event. Uniqueness and referential integrity are maintained by the backend with respect to admin accounts and target entities.

target_type.description: Type of the entity the moderation action is performed on. Accepted values: "article", "comment", "attachment". Controls which UUID should be supplied in target_id and determines how moderation is tracked.

target_id.description: UUID of the item moderated—this can refer to an article, comment, or attachment depending on target_type. Used for polymorphic resolution in moderation logs.

action.description: Moderation action performed (e.g., "remove", "edit", "ban"). Must match one of the allowed moderation command vocabulary items enforced by the backend.

reason.description: Reason provided by the admin for this moderation action. Required for audit completeness and compliance review.

outcome.description: Result or effect after moderation (e.g., "deleted", "edited", "banned", "restored"). Must conform to allowed values defined by moderation policy.

created_at.description: Timestamp when this moderation action was performed (UTC, ISO 8601). Required for audit accuracy. Backend may verify time within acceptable range.

IDiscussionBoardModerationLog.IUpdate.description:
DTO for updating permitted fields of an existing moderation log record. Only rationale/justification (reason) and outcome can be corrected per audit policies. All primary event attributes (target_type, target_id, action, created_at, admin_id) remain immutable and are not included in this schema.

This type allows the system or authorized admin to amend or clarify the historical record of a moderation action for compliance needs. Deletion or update of core event data is strictly forbidden, preserving log integrity.

reason.description: Optional updated rationale for the moderation event. May clarify or append context for audit review.

outcome.description: Optional updated outcome or resolution after moderation. Used to clarify the final state after further administrative review.

id.description:
Primary Key. Universally unique file identifier for attachment record.

Serves as the canonical reference for this file metadata in all business operations and audit trails.

original_filename.description: Original filename as submitted by user; displayed in download links. Preserves the name provided on file upload.

storage_filename.description: Internal reference or generated filename used for storage (server, cloud bucket, etc.), never exposed to the user. Ensures collision-free and unguessable storage location.

size_bytes.description: Exact file size in bytes as stored. Used to validate application and storage constraints (max 10 MB per requirements).

mime_type.description: IANA MIME type of the uploaded file (e.g., 'image/png', 'application/pdf'). Required for attachment accept/serve validation and display.

checksum_sha256.description: SHA-256 hash checksum of file content, used for duplicate detection, integrity verification, and security audit logging. Uniqueness enforces single storage per identical file.

storage_location.description: Provider identifier or physical/cloud storage reference (e.g., S3 bucket, server path, etc.). Used exclusively by backend for file I/O routing. Not visible to application frontends.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp of attachment deletion (soft delete). Null if active; set when attachment is removed, orphaned, or expunged. Supports compliance and orphan cleanup workflows.

created_at.description: File metadata creation timestamp. Set on initial upload and immutable thereafter for audit/compliance purposes.

updated_at.description: File metadata last modification timestamp. Updated on any admin or system change to technical information (not business linkage).

IDiscussionBoardAttachment.description:
Technical metadata and storage abstraction for all uploaded attachments (images, files) in the discussion board platform.

This object is the canonical record for any attachment appearing in articles, comments, or future extensible features. It encapsulates all security, integrity, and storage information for the uploaded file, decoupled from business entity references.

Every property is designed to support high-assurance file handling, audit, deduplication, and compliance with upload/storage policies. Soft deletion and audit fields enable robust lifecycle and regulatory management.

Directly maps to the discussion_board_attachments Prisma table. All business associations and linkage are handled elsewhere.

Use this schema for read-only output or administrative views; do not expose internal storage information to unprivileged clients.

page.description: Page number for pagination. Starts from 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of items per page (up to 100 allowed).

search.description: Search query for partial match on original filename. Optional. Matches substrings in original file names.

mime_type.description: Filter attachments by IANA MIME type (e.g., 'image/png', 'application/pdf'). Optional.

deleted.description: Whether to include only deleted (soft-deleted) attachments. True for only deleted, false for only active, unset for all.

size_min.description: Lower bound filter for file size in bytes. Optional.

size_max.description: Upper bound filter for file size in bytes. Optional. Must be larger or equal to size_min if both are set.

created_from.description: Lower bound filter for created_at timestamp (inclusive, ISO 8601 format). Optional.

created_to.description: Upper bound filter for created_at timestamp (inclusive, ISO 8601 format). Optional.

oneOf.description: Field by which to sort the attachments. Allowed: 'created_at', 'size_bytes', 'original_filename'.
Field by which to sort the attachments. Allowed: 'created_at', 'size_bytes', 'original_filename'.
Field by which to sort the attachments. Allowed: 'created_at', 'size_bytes', 'original_filename'.

sort_by.description: Field by which to sort the attachments. Allowed: 'created_at', 'size_bytes', 'original_filename'.

oneOf.description: Order of sorting: ascending ('asc') or descending ('desc').
Order of sorting: ascending ('asc') or descending ('desc').

order.description: Order of sorting: ascending ('asc') or descending ('desc').

IDiscussionBoardAttachment.IRequest.description:
Filtering and pagination parameters for querying attachment records.

Supports searching by original filename, filtering by MIME type, file size, date ranges, and deletion status, as well as sorting and pagination controls. Designed for administrative and audit endpoints traversing the technical attachment inventory.

All fields are optional; only set desired filters, sorting, and pagination parameters. Defaults may apply if not provided.

IDiscussionBoardAttachment.ICreate.description:
DTO for registering a new attachment in the discussion board platform. Used to record file and storage metadata when an image or document is uploaded by admins. This type captures the necessary technical information for file reconciliation, deduplication, and compliance, following strict normalization outlined in the underlying database.

All business-related associations (article, comment linkage) are managed separately. The file's binary data is not uploaded via this DTO; only metadata is recorded. Fields include user-facing and storage-internal filenames, file size, MIME type, file checksum for deduplication/security, and the storage provider reference. Compliance with required types, allowed MIME types, and file size limits is validated at the business logic and API layers—not within the DTO itself. System-managed fields (id, audit timestamps, deletion marker) are generated by the backend and excluded from writes.

original_filename.description: Original filename as submitted by the user when uploading the file. This name is preserved for use in download links and UI display, but is not used for storage or internal reference.

storage_filename.description: Generated or internal filename uniquely identifying this file within its storage provider/bucket. Never revealed to the frontend. Ensures that uploaded file storage locations are collision-free and unpredictable.

size_bytes.description: Exact file size in bytes as stored by the provider. Used to enforce application- and storage-level constraints and for compliance checks (e.g., 10MB limit).

mime_type.description: IANA MIME type of the uploaded file, such as 'image/png', 'application/pdf', etc. This value is required for performing validation at upload and correct handling by consumers.

checksum_sha256.description: SHA-256 cryptographic hash of the file contents. Used to validate uniqueness, ensure integrity, prevent duplicates, and support compliance audit. Backend enforces uniqueness at database layer per requirements.

storage_location.description: Opaque identifier for the physical or logical storage (e.g., bucket, server, or location key) used for this file. Populated by backend at upload after storage provider is determined.

IDiscussionBoardAttachment.IUpdate.description:
DTO for updating permitted technical metadata of an attachment record in the discussion board system. Used by authorized administrators to modify backend storage references or correct technical metadata for uploaded files/images.

Only technical fields are editable; identity (id), cryptographic signature (checksum_sha256), and creation timestamp (created_at) cannot be changed. File content and business associations are managed externally. Changes are tracked using updated_at for compliance and troubleshooting purposes. All validation logic concerning field mutability, value correctness, and audit controls must be enforced by application and service logic, not directly by the DTO.

original_filename.description: Original filename that may be mutable only for technical correction (typically immutable).

storage_filename.description: Backend storage reference to the actual file location. May be updated if moved/corrected (e.g., renaming or consolidating storage buckets).

size_bytes.description: File size in bytes. Editable only for file system corrections or integrity rechecks.

mime_type.description: IANA MIME type for updated/corrected technical information. Enforced at application logic.

storage_location.description: Storage provider reference or bucket/location string. Allows backend migrations or provider changes. Abstracted from any direct file operation.

IDiscussionBoardSystemConfig.ISummary.description:
Summary type for board-level system configuration settings.

Represents a single configuration item as retrieved from the board's global settings table. Provides the unique key, value, and metadata needed for administrative UIs or for showing active configuration to API consumers. Used for list views, dashboards, and config management pages where only summary info is required. For detailed configuration (including history or extended audit), use the full IDiscussionBoardSystemConfig type.

This type omits system-reserved management fields except those relevant for listing configuration state and doesn't expose operational audit log detail.

id.description:
Unique identifier for this configuration setting entry.

Mapped from the 'id' column in Prisma schema; globally unique UUID for every board system config.

config_key.description:
Unique key identifying the configuration item. Example: 'feature_upload_enabled', 'max_file_size_mb'. Required for addressing, display, and programmatic lookups.

Taken from 'config_key' in Prisma schema, which enforces uniqueness per setting for board-wide parameters.

config_value.description:
Current value for this configuration item as a string. Can be a plain scalar (e.g., true/false, number as string) or a serialized object/JSON string depending on the config domain.

Always reflects the most recent value stored. See board documentation for allowed value types for each key.

description.description:
Optional human-readable explanation of this setting's business purpose, for display in admin UI or config summary pages.

Mapped from the nullable 'description' column; can be null if undocumented or reserved.

created_at.description:
Timestamp of initial creation.

Used for audit and config lifecycle tracking. See 'created_at' in Prisma schema.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of last configuration update, not including soft deletion.

Useful for tracking recency and supporting config timelines. Sourced from 'updated_at' in Prisma schema.

deleted_at.description:
Nullable timestamp indicating when this configuration entry was softened/deprecated or flagged as inactive.

Corresponds to 'deleted_at' in Prisma. Null means the config is currently active. If set, UI should mark value as inactive or for archival display.

IDiscussionBoardUser.ISummary.description:
Summary DTO for standard discussion board user identity.

Represents a minimal, public-facing view of a registered user account for display in lists or UI contexts requiring only essential non-sensitive attributes. Intended for list and attribution displays (e.g., showing article authorship, comment ownership) and does not reveal authentication or private account information.

Note: All fields here are safe for public exposure and exclude authentication secrets and audit trail details.

id.description: Unique user identity; UUID as primary key per Prisma schema. Required for entity linking, attribution, and strong user references.

email.description:
User's registered email address (serves as natural key). Used for username displays or user identification in admin contexts. Always unique as enforced by schema constraints.

Never reveal password, password_hash, or other secrets in this summary type. This field is safe for admin/management contexts only.

created_at.description: Timestamp of initial user registration. For audit and lifecycle tracking. Sourced directly from 'created_at' in Prisma table.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of latest material change to this user (e.g., email or password update). Used for change auditing; see 'updated_at'.

deleted_at.description: Nullable timestamp for soft delete; shows logical removal (user-initiated or admin action). If null, account is active.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.ISummary.description:
Summary data for a user-generated discussion article.

Contains only essential fields for list displays, previews, and lightweight embedding.
Provides identifying, authorship, and main audit information, but avoids full content, attachments, or deep relations for performance reasons.

Used for search results, feed/list API responses, scoreboards, and minimal references. Based on the discussion_board_articles Prisma model.

Belongs-to reference: user is represented as IDiscussionBoardUser.ISummary to provide context in summary views. All BELONGS-TO relations in summary types must use .ISummary DTOs for context.

id.description: Unique identifier for the article. Automatically generated on creation.

title.description: Title of the article. Limited to 200 characters, supports only sanitized text.

user.description:
The author of this article. References the BELONGS-TO user entity.

Transformed from user_id string per summary relation rule: summary must include BELONGS-TO reference as object, not just raw ID.

created_at.description: Datetime when the article was created (ISO 8601 UTC). Immutable once set.

updated_at.description: Datetime when the article was last updated.

IDiscussionBoardArticleAttachment.ISumma.description:
Summary information for a single file or image attached to a discussion board article.

Represents the metadata required for clients to display attachment lists or details for articles, including file type, storage URI, and administrative context. Records are always subordinate to a parent article and reference the owning article via its .ISummary object, never as a raw UUID. This summary intentionally omits sensitive URIs or internal processing fields and focuses on what is relevant for display and audit.

Relationship: Always belongs to a single article, which is now included via the article: IDiscussionBoardArticle.ISummary object. Business logic enforces allowed file types and size limits, with soft deletion indicated via the nullable deleted_at field.

id.description: Primary key for the attachment record. Unique across all board attachments.

article.description:
The article this attachment belongs to (BELONGS-TO relation).

Transformed from article_id string to reference object per summary relation rule: summary must include BELONGS-TO reference as object, not just raw ID.

file_name.description: Original file name (as uploaded by user), including file extension.

mime_type.description: Attachment MIME type, such as 'image/jpeg', 'application/pdf'. Strictly validated by system rules.

file_size.description: Size of the attachment in bytes. Maximum allowed is 10MB per business rules.

file_uri.description: Permanent storage URI for the file (could be S3 bucket, CDN, or internal path per configuration). Not directly exposed to unauthenticated users.

created_at.description: Timestamp the attachment record was created/uploaded.

deleted_at.description: Soft delete timestamp, nullable. Set if attachment was removed by user or moderation, otherwise null.

A page.

Collection of records with pagination information.

IDiscussionBoardArticleComment.description:
Represents a single user comment posted beneath an article on the economic or political discussion board.

Each comment is linked to a parent article and an author (registered user), represented as summary references for complete context. Comments are text-only (no attachments or nesting), and can be edited or soft deleted (deleted_at present) by their author or by administrators. A full version history is maintained for moderation and audit. The entity supports flat, chronological discussions.

Relationships include summary references to the discussion article and author user entity (association relations). Lifecycle timestamps show creation, last update, and soft deletion where applicable.

id.description: Primary key (UUID) uniquely identifying this comment.

author.description: Reference to the author (registered user) who posted the comment. Uses summary type for safe context embedding.

article.description: Reference to the parent article this comment belongs to. Uses summary type for reference context.

body.description: Comment content as provided by the author. Must contain non-blank text and not exceed 5,000 characters per business constraints.

created_at.description: Timestamp when this comment was originally posted. Immutable—automatically set on insertion.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the last update to this comment. Automatically refreshed on edit.

oneOf.description: If present, indicates the timestamp when this comment was hidden or soft-deleted. Null if the comment is currently visible.
Null means comment is not deleted.

deleted_at.description: The timestamp of deletion or null if active.

IDiscussionBoardArticleComment.IRequest.description:
Request schema for searching and paginating discussion board comments across articles. 

Supports keyword body search, filtering by article, author, creation and update date ranges, and deleted state. Pagination and advanced querying fields can be extended for performance and moderation use cases. Used as request body in /discussionBoard/comments PATCH operation; all filters are optional but support strongly typed UUIDs where appropriate.

Reflects business rules for discussion_board_comments querying and index utilization. Designed for efficiency in user and admin comment navigation workflows.

body.description: Keyword search filter for comment body text. Matches using GIN index; optional for full-text/body search scenarios.

discussion_board_article_id.description: Filter to comments belonging to the specified article (discussion_board_articles.id). Optional for article-scoped searches.

discussion_board_user_id.description: Filter to comments authored by the specified user (discussion_board_users.id). Optional for author-scoped or user moderation views.

created_from.description: Lower bound for comment creation timestamp (inclusive). Only comments created on or after this datetime will be included.

created_to.description: Upper bound for comment creation timestamp (inclusive). Only comments created on or before this datetime will be included.

updated_from.description: Lower bound for comment update timestamp. Only comments updated on or after this datetime will be included.

updated_to.description: Upper bound for comment update timestamp. Only comments updated on or before this datetime will be included.

deleted.description: Filter by soft-deleted state. True to include only deleted comments, false to include only active comments, omitted for both. Used in admin moderation views.

page.description: Pagination: page number. Defaults to 1 if omitted in API implementation.

limit.description: Pagination: maximum number of comments per page. Maximum is 100.

IDiscussionBoardArticleComment.ICreate.description:
Request body type for creating a new comment beneath an article in the discussion board platform.

Requires a non-empty comment body (max 5,000 characters), the target article's identifier, and the author identifier as per business rules. The article and user IDs must reference valid, existing parent entities. All required fields are validated for presence and integrity. Actor user ID is obtained from the session context for authenticated users.

Timestamps are set automatically; the client does not and must not supply created_at, updated_at, or deleted_at. The response will echo the new comment using the IDiscussionBoardComment type.

discussion_board_article_id.description: Reference to the parent article for this comment. Must match the id of an existing discussion_board_articles record.

body.description: Comment body (text content). Must be non-empty and must not exceed 5,000 characters per business rules.

IDiscussionBoardArticleComment.IUpdate.description:
Request body type for updating the text content of an existing comment on a discussion board article.

Only the text body may be modified; all other fields—including article reference, author, and timestamps—are immutable and controlled by the server. Edits are subject to validation and are tracked in a companion snapshot table for audit/compliance purposes.

To update: provide the new content as 'body'. The value must be a non-empty string, and cannot exceed 5,000 characters. Updates from unauthorized actors or for a comment in a deleted state are denied by business and permission logic.

body.description: New text content for the comment. Must not be empty, and may not exceed 5,000 characters.

IDiscussionBoardArticleComment.ISummary.description:
Summary schema for a single comment displayed beneath discussion board articles.

Provides direct context by embedding both the user (author) and parent article as .ISummary objects—in compliance with relation transformation and atomic operation principles. Used in comment lists, notifications, and summary views. Includes timestamps for publication, update, and deletion for UI, audit, and lifecycle management.

- `author`: Minimal user identity summarizing the comment's creator, avoids exposure of raw foreign keys.
- `article`: Minimal article summary for display context; enables rendering without leaking FK UUIDs.

Flat comment model—no nesting, no self-reference, no aggregations (only single-level comments).

id.description: Unique, immutable primary key identifying this comment.

author.description: User who created (authored) this comment. Provided as an .ISummary reference for contextual display without exposing foreign key UUIDs.

article.description: Minimal reference to the parent article associated with this comment, following the .ISummary pattern.

body.description: Text content of the comment (author-provided). Limited to 5,000 characters per business rule.

created_at.description: Timestamp of initial comment creation (ISO-8601 UTC).

updated_at.description: Timestamp of most recent comment update/edit (ISO-8601 UTC).

deleted_at.description: Nullable: null if comment is live; timestamp if comment has been soft deleted.
